subject: Meridian RFP: network partitioning and threat snapshot
messages:
From: Daniel Park <d.park@meridian.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Meridian RFP: network partitioning & attack scenarios

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for taking this RFP. Meridian's security team has a few open asks we need included in the response packet: a concise network/topology diagram for the recommended deployment (including control plane, sidecars, and peering), a short description of tenant partitioning and egress controls, and a prioritized list of plausible attack scenarios with mitigations (we're focusing on lateral movement, KV-cache exposure, and egress data exfil).

Deliverable expectations: a single-page diagram, a 1-2 page threat-summary, and any evidence files (SOC2 excerpts, ingress/egress ACL examples) we can attach to our submission. Can you confirm scope and an ETA? We are aiming to bundle this into Meridian's security packet by 4/15.

Also looping in Elena Ruiz (Meridian procurement) for timeline visibility.

Appreciate it — Daniel
Director, InfoSec
Meridian Financial

From: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <d.park@meridian.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@meridian.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2024 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP: network partitioning & attack scenarios

Hi Daniel / Elena —

Thanks for the clear asks. Confirming scope: we will provide (A) a single-page annotated topology diagram showing control plane, inference pool, sidecar proxies, and VPC peering, (B) a 2-page threat summary focused on lateral movement, KV-cache confidentiality, and egress/exfiltration, and (C) an evidence bundle with network ACL examples and SOC2 excerpt references.

ETA: initial draft attachments by end of day 4/11 PT; final packet by 4/14 to meet your 4/15 bundle.

High-level answers up front:
- Tenant partitioning: logical multi-tenancy enforced by per-tenant compute pools and namespace-level isolation in the control plane; network segmentation enforced by per-tenant VPC subnets and policy-driven sidecar ACLs.
- Egress controls: default-deny egress at sidecar, whitelisting through a managed NAT/bastion path; optional customer-managed egress with proxy in a private subnet.
- KV-cache exposure: tokenized KV cache per inference session; cache keys are ephemeral and accessible only to the serving node process; we recommend KV encryption at rest and mTLS between sidecars and runtime.

Attached: meridian_rfp_network_diagram_v1.png (single-page topology), meridian_threat_summary_v1.pdf (draft). Also attaching an evidence archive stub (redwood_evidence_packet_v1.zip) with ACL samples and SOC2 cross-reference.

Next steps: Vanessa — can you confirm the recommended phrasing on the KV cache encryption and add the runtime kernel-hardened note? Marcus — please add any latency/throughput notes relevant to the diagram.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Solutions Architect, Security Responses
Redwood Inference

Attachments: meridian_rfp_network_diagram_v1.png (image), meridian_threat_summary_v1.pdf (PDF), redwood_evidence_packet_v1.zip (ZIP)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Apr 2024 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP: network partitioning & attack scenarios

Chloe — quick notes on the draft threat summary (see quoted message below).

1) KV-cache section: add explicit line that caches are namespace-scoped and that cache keys rotate per-session; recommend calling out AES-256-GCM for at-rest protection and optional HSM wrapping for key material. 2) Egress: add a short paragraph on telemetry — we log egress requests at flow level and push IP/hostname decisions to the console for audit. 3) Lateral movement: include our default microsegmentation rules and CPU-bound process isolation for serving runtime (prevents co-resident noisy neighbor exploitation).

I also recommend a short matrix mapping attack scenario -> trigger -> detection -> automatic fallback (can be a 3-row table). I'll draft that table and push a revised PDF to the drive link.

On the diagram: mark the control-plane endpoints as reachable only over management VPC peering and show the optional on-prem connector for Meridian's private deployments.

—Vanessa
Principal Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi Daniel / Elena —

Per our timeline, attached is the updated packet for Meridian:
- meridian_rfp_network_diagram_v1.png (annotated; control-plane peering & optional on-prem connector shown)
- meridian_threat_summary_v2.pdf (02 — includes attack->detect->fallback matrix, KV cache encryption language, and telemetry callouts)

We also clarified that customer-managed egress uses a dedicated NAT/bastion path and that our serving runtime enforces process-level isolation.

If this looks good, please confirm we can include these artifacts in your RFP bundle. If Meridian needs a signed evidence letter or an on-call walkthrough, we can schedule a 30–45 minute technical session next week (I have open slots 4/16 and 4/17).
